title: Optimal Substructure Invariants in a Zig-Based Multimodal Travel Planner for a 228,060-Edge Graph
topic: Engineering a Multimodal Travel Planner on a 228,060-Edge Graph

abstract: We present a lightweight, mode-aware path engine implemented in Zig that computes shortest multimodal routes on a 228,060-edge urban graph. The engine augments a standard adjacency array with a mode tag and applies Dijkstra's algorithm restricted to user-supplied mode sets. We formally prove that the returned path satisfies the optimal substructure invariant and that the algorithm runs in $O(|V|+|E|)$ for traversal and $O((|V|+|E|)\log |V|)$ for relaxation. Static analysis of the source yields 164 SLOC and eight function blocks, confirming the modest code footprint. No empirical runtime measurements are reported; all claims are supported by formal proofs and AST inspection. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/zig-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261018_210120_engineering_a_multimodal_trave}
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
